summary.text: Assuming the claimed eventual relation, the shifted pairs \((a_{3773+t}+1,a_{3774+t}+1)\) follow the Fibonacci transition \((x,y)\mapsto(y,x+y)\); modular exponentiation modulo \(p=195318521017\), from the computed initial residues \((77940394259,99768150822)\), yields \((1,1)\) at \(t=249580073233\), so \(p\) divides both \(a_{249580077006}\) and \(a_{249580077007}\). Their gcd is therefore greater than one, making the defining recurrence give \(a_{249580077008}\le a_{249580077007}+a_{249580077006}\), contrary to the claimed value one larger than this sum.

full_proof.text:
Let \((a_n)_{n\geq 1}\) be defined by
\[
a_1=a_2=1,
\qquad
a_n=g_n+\frac{a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}}{g_n}\quad(n\geq3),
\qquad
g_n=\gcd(a_{n-1},a_{n-2}).
\]
The quotient is an integer because \(g_n\) divides both preceding terms. We will disprove the conjecture by showing that its first asserted identity cannot hold for every \(n\geq3775\). Since the conjecture asserts all three identities simultaneously, disproving the first one is enough.

Set
\[
p=195318521017,
\qquad R=249580073233,
\qquad N=3775+R=249580077008.
\]
No primality property of \(p\) is needed; only \(p\geq2\) will matter.

We argue by contradiction. Suppose that the conjecture is true. In particular, suppose
\[
a_n=1+a_{n-1}+a_{n-2} \tag{1}
\]
for every \(n\geq3775\). We will use (1) through index \(N-1\) to prove that \(p\) divides both \(a_{N-2}\) and \(a_{N-1}\). The defining gcd recurrence will then imply that (1) is false at index \(N\), giving the contradiction.

First we record the finite calculation of the sequence up to indices 3773 and 3774. It can be performed entirely with integer arithmetic by starting with the pair \((x,y)=(1,1)\) and repeating
\[
g:=\gcd(x,y),\qquad (x,y):=\left(y,\,g+\frac{x+y}{g}\right).
\]
After \(k\) repetitions the pair is \((a_{k+1},a_{k+2})\). After 3772 repetitions this gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{3773}={}&,\\
a_{3774}={}&.
\end{aligned}
\]
Reducing these two integers plus 1 modulo \(p\) gives
\[
a_{3773}+1\equiv77940394259\pmod p,
\qquad
a_{3774}+1\equiv99768150822\pmod p. \tag{2}
\]
For reproducibility, the corresponding quotient-remainder calculations are
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{3773}+1={}&p\cdot
\\
&+77940394259,
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{3774}+1={}&p\cdot
\\
&+99768150822.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus (2) is a direct finite consequence of the defining recurrence.

We next encode the propagation forced by (1). Work modulo \(p\), and consider formal pairs \((x,y)\), with multiplication
\[
(x,y)(u,v)= igl(xu+yv,\;xv+yu+yv\bigr)\pmod p. \tag{3}
\]
This is simply multiplication of the formal expressions \(x+y\tau\) and \(u+v\tau\), subject to
\[
\tau^2=1+\tau.
\]
Consequently this multiplication is associative and commutative, with identity \((1,0)\), and \(\tau\) itself is represented by \((0,1)\). In particular,
\[
(0,1)(x,y)=(y,x+y). \tag{4}
\]

For \(t\geq0\), define the shifted pair
\[
B_t=(a_{3773+t}+1,\;a_{3774+t}+1)\pmod p.
\]
Applying (1) at \(n=3775+t\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{3775+t}+1
 &=2+a_{3774+t}+a_{3773+t}\\
 &=(a_{3774+t}+1)+(a_{3773+t}+1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Using (4), it follows that
\[
B_{t+1}=\tau B_t. \tag{5}
\]
By induction on \(t\),
\[
B_t=\tau^t B_0. \tag{6}
\]
Notice that deriving (6) for \(t=R\) uses (1) only at the indices \(3775,3776,\ldots,3774+R=N-1\), not at \(N\) itself.

It remains to compute \(\tau^R B_0\) modulo \(p\). The following square-and-multiply table supplies the complete modular computation. Each pair in the table denotes the coordinates of \(\tau^e\) under multiplication (3). When the next exponent is twice the preceding exponent, the next pair is obtained by squaring; when it is one more, it is obtained by multiplying by \(\tau=(0,1)\). All coordinates are reduced to the interval \([0,p-1]\).

For example, the first few lines express
\[
\tau^2=(1,1),\quad \tau^3=(1,2),\quad
\tau^6=(1,2)^2=(5,8),
\]
and every later line follows from exactly the same multiplication formula (3). The sequence of exponents is the recursive binary addition chain for \(R\), so the final line establishes
\[
\tau^R=(117378126758,21827756563)\pmod p. \tag{7}
\]

By (2),
\[
B_0=(77940394259,99768150822)\pmod p.
\]
Multiplying this by (7) using (3), the unreduced first coordinate is
\[
117378126758\cdot77940394259
 +21827756563\cdot99768150822
 =11326212385784681827108
 =57988419771p+1.
\]
The unreduced second coordinate is
\[
\begin{aligned}
&117378126758\cdot99768150822
 +21827756563\cdot77940394259
 +21827756563\cdot99768150822\\
&\hspace{25mm}=15589577514788957011679
 =79816176334p+1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
\tau^R B_0=(1,1)\pmod p. \tag{8}
\]
Combining (6) and (8) gives
\[
B_R=(1,1)\pmod p.
\]
By the definition of \(B_R\), this says
\[
a_{3773+R}+1\equiv1\pmod p,
\qquad
a_{3774+R}+1\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
Hence
\[
p\mid a_{3773+R}=a_{N-2},
\qquad
p\mid a_{3774+R}=a_{N-1}. \tag{9}
\]

We now show why (9) makes the claimed identity impossible at the next index. First, every sequence term is positive. This follows by induction: \(a_1=a_2=1\), and if the preceding terms are positive, then their gcd is positive, so the defining expression
\[
g+\frac{a+b}{g}
\]
is positive.

Put
\[
a=a_{N-1},\qquad b=a_{N-2},\qquad g=\gcd(a,b).
\]
By (9), \(p\mid g\). Since \(p\geq2\), we have \(g\geq2\). Also, because \(a,b>0\) and \(g\) divides both, \(g\leq a\) and \(g\leq b\). Thus
\[
2g\leq a+b,
\qquad	ext{so}\qquad
g\leq\left\lfloor\frac{a+b}{2}\right\rfloor.
\]
Since \(g\geq2\), division by \(g\) gives no larger an integer quotient than division by 2:
\[
\left\lfloor\frac{a+b}{g}\right\rfloor
 \leq \left\lfloor\frac{a+b}{2}\right\rfloor.
\]
Consequently the actual recurrence gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_N
 &=g+\frac{a+b}{g}\\
 &\leq 2\left\lfloor\frac{a+b}{2}\right\rfloor\\
 &\leq a+b. \tag{10}
\end{aligned}
\]
On the other hand, the conjectured first identity (1), applied at \(N=249580077008\geq3775\), says
\[
a_N=1+a+b>a+b, \tag{11}
\]
contradicting (10).

Thus it is impossible that the identity \(a_n=1+a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}\) hold for every \(n\geq3775\). In particular, the conjunction claiming that, for every such \(n\), this identity and the two additional identities
\[
a_n=2a_{n-1}-a_{n-3}
\]
and
\[
a_n=(a_{3774}+1)F_{n-3772}-(a_{3772}+1)F_{n-3774}-1
\]
all hold is false. This disproves the stated conjecture.
